facts.content: Patient reports difficulty breathing after an insect sting or bite.
facts.source_text: Chief Complaint: Difficulty breathing after insect sting/bite

facts.content: A 27-year-old male reports difficulty breathing and mild swelling of the lips following an insect sting on the right arm that occurred minutes ago.
facts.source_text: 27-year-old male reports difficulty breathing and mild swelling of lips following an insect sting (likely wasp or bee) on the right arm minutes ago.

facts.content: The patient notes a localized rash and slight soreness at the sting site.
facts.source_text: Patient notes a localized rash and slight soreness at sting site.

facts.content: The patient denies acute severe breathing difficulty at present but feels anxious that symptoms may worsen.
facts.source_text: Denies acute severe breathing difficulty currently but feels anxious that symptoms may worsen.

facts.content: The patient has no prior history of anaphylaxis or need for epinephrine.
facts.source_text: No prior history of anaphylaxis or need for epinephrine (EpiPen).

facts.content: The patient has previous eczema and is allergic to penicillin.
facts.source_text: Has previous eczema; allergic to penicillin.

facts.content: The patient has occasional anxiety or panic attacks but has not received treatment.
facts.source_text: Has occasional anxiety/panic attacks but no treatment.

facts.content: Respiratory review notes a sensation of difficulty breathing that is not acute at present.
facts.source_text: Respiratory: Difficulty breathing sensation (not acute at present)

facts.content: Skin review notes a rash localized to the arm sting site that is slightly red with no significant swelling.
facts.source_text: Skin: Rash localized to arm sting site, slightly red, no significant swelling

facts.content: The patient reports no history of food or pet allergies.
facts.source_text: No history of food or pet allergies reported

facts.content: The patient reports no fever or systemic symptoms.
facts.source_text: No reported fever or systemic symptoms

facts.content: The patient has a history of eczema.
facts.source_text: Eczema

facts.content: The patient has occasional untreated anxiety.
facts.source_text: Anxiety (occasional, untreated)

facts.content: The patient is not using any medications for this episode.
facts.source_text: None currently used for this episode

facts.content: The patient has not taken any antihistamines yet.
facts.source_text: No antihistamines taken yet

facts.content: Over-the-counter chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablets are recommended, one tablet up to six times per day as needed.
facts.source_text: Recommend oral antihistamines: over-the-counter chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet, 1 tablet up to six times per day as needed

facts.content: A once-daily formulation of an antihistamine is acceptable as an alternative.
facts.source_text: or once daily formulation is acceptable.

facts.content: The patient is allergic to penicillin, with reaction not specified.
facts.source_text: Penicillin (reaction not specified)

facts.content: There is no relevant family history of allergies or acute reactions.
facts.source_text: No relevant family history of allergies or acute reactions

facts.content: The patient works as a computer scientist.
facts.source_text: Occupation: Computer scientist

facts.content: The patient lives alone.
facts.source_text: Lives alone

facts.content: The patient has a pet cat.
facts.source_text: Has a pet cat

facts.content: No known substance use is documented for the patient.
facts.source_text: No known substance use documented

facts.content: On general examination, the patient is alert, conversant, and in no observed distress.
facts.source_text: General: Alert, conversant, no distress observed

facts.content: HEENT exam shows lips appearing normal with no obvious swelling and no mucosal or airway swelling on remote inspection of the oral cavity and throat; soft tissues are clear.
facts.source_text: HEENT: Lips appear normal, no obvious swelling; oral cavity and throat inspected remotely with patient cooperation—no mucosal or airway swelling; soft tissues clear

facts.content: Respiratory exam shows normal breathing at the time of consult with no stridor or respiratory distress.
facts.source_text: Respiratory: Breathing normal at time of consult, no stridor or respiratory distress noted

facts.content: Skin exam shows a slightly red rash on the right arm at the sting site with no significant swelling and a visible puncture mark without signs of infection, warmth, or spreading.
facts.source_text: Skin: Rash on right arm; slightly red, no significant swelling; puncture mark visible, no signs of infection (no warmth or spreading)

facts.content: The primary diagnosis is a localized allergic reaction to an insect sting, likely wasp or bee.
facts.source_text: 1. Localized allergic reaction to insect sting (likely wasp or bee)

facts.content: The reaction consists of mild rash and soreness at the sting site with subjective mild breathing difficulty and anxiety but no objective signs of anaphylaxis or airway compromise and no current life-threatening allergic reaction.
facts.source_text: Mild rash and soreness at sting site with subjective mild breathing difficulty and anxiety but no objective signs of anaphylaxis or airway compromise. No current life-threatening allergic reaction.

facts.content: The patient has occasional untreated anxiety, which may contribute to the sensation of breathing difficulty and distress.
facts.source_text:
2. Anxiety (occasional, untreated)
   May contribute to sensation of breathing difficulty and patient distress.

facts.content: The patient has a known penicillin allergy.
facts.source_text: 3. Penicillin allergy, status known

facts.content: For the localized allergic reaction to insect sting, oral antihistamines such as over-the-counter chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablets are recommended, one tablet up to six times daily as needed or an acceptable once-daily formulation.
facts.source_text: Recommend oral antihistamines: over-the-counter chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet, 1 tablet up to six times per day as needed or once daily formulation is acceptable.

facts.content: The patient is educated on signs of severe allergic reaction including swelling of lips, tongue, throat, difficulty breathing, and stridor, and instructed to seek immediate emergency care if symptoms worsen acutely.
facts.source_text: Educate patient on signs of severe allergic reaction including swelling of lips, tongue, throat, difficulty breathing, stridor. Instruct to seek immediate emergency care if symptoms worsen acutely.

facts.content: The patient is advised to monitor the sting site for spreading redness, warmth, or infection and to consider antibiotics if infection develops.
facts.source_text: Advise to monitor sting site for signs of spreading redness, warmth, or infection; consider antibiotics if infection develops.

facts.content: Patient education material on anaphylaxis awareness is to be provided.
facts.source_text: Provide patient education material on anaphylaxis awareness.

facts.content: No urgent allergy testing or epinephrine is deemed needed at this time due to absence of severe symptoms.
facts.source_text: No urgent allergy testing or epinephrine needed at this time due to absence of severe symptoms.

facts.content: For anxiety, the patient is reassured and it is explained that symptoms are likely related to a mild local reaction and anxiety.
facts.source_text: Reassure patient; explain symptoms likely related to mild local reaction and anxiety.

facts.content: The patient is encouraged to contact the provider for ongoing concerns or worsening symptoms.
facts.source_text: Encourage contact with provider for ongoing concerns or worsening symptoms.

facts.content: The patient will remain at home with no immediate hospital referral.
facts.source_text: Patient remains at home; no immediate hospital referral needed.

facts.content: The patient is to follow up if symptoms worsen or recur.
facts.source_text: Patient to follow up if symptoms worsen or recur.

facts.content: The patient is instructed to go to the emergency department immediately if there is rapid progression of symptoms, especially breathing difficulty or swelling.
facts.source_text: Immediate emergency department visit if rapid progression of symptoms, especially breathing difficulty or swelling.
